forces.name: Till we both have ours
forces.increment_logic: When the others carry through what they take on and stay with a shared task until it is done, I expect them to stay with me until my share of it is in hand, and to come when I ask a hand with the next one: my sense that help here comes back to me rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When the others drop what they take on and drift off once their own part is paid, I expect them to be gone when I need a hand to finish mine, and an ask of mine to go unanswered: my sense that help here comes back to me falls.
forces.explanation: By three, children who have made a joint commitment protest when a partner breaks off and acknowledge their own leaving (Grafenhain, Behne, Carpenter and Tomasello 2009), and they keep working at a joint task after their own reward is in hand until the partner has theirs, less so when the task was not joint (Hamann, Warneken and Tomasello 2012). After collaborating, three-year-olds divide the spoils more equally than after a windfall or parallel work (Hamann et al. 2011). In young children, carrying one's part and seeing the partner home are one commitment, so a member's reading of whether the others carry their parts is also a reading of whether they will be there when her own need falls due. The evidence is children's behaviour toward one partner in a dyadic task; the step to an adult member's felt expectation that help comes back from the group is the model's, so keep the card modest and scale it to how far the work is joint. Nil for work each does alone. Distinct from Good for Their Word (E:Reciprocity->OutResp), which runs the other way, and from Quality Street (E:OutResp->GrpProsp), which reads capability. Where E:Engagement->Reciprocity circumstance one fires on the same scene, play this card small. Forms a Reinforce loop with E:Reciprocity->OutResp; the brake is a need plainly met or unmet, scored by play.

era.why: The core of both ends is non-verbal: staying with a joint task until each has their share, or leaving once one's own is in hand, and expecting help or none in return. Tomasello's interdependence account places this collaborative commitment in early human foraging before language, though chimpanzees show it weakly. Today it may be spoken.

forces.name: Fondness softens a breach

forces.decrement_logic: When I am fond of the members, a breach of one of the group's conventions by one of them reads first as a slip, and my indignation at the breach eases a little.
forces.explanation: Group level only: fondness for the members as a whole, never for one member. Leniency towards those we like is supported: people anticipate protecting close others who commit even severe wrongs (Weidman et al. 2020), and views of a person's character colour blame (Alicke 1992). Both are evidence about individuals, so the group-level step is adjacent and the card plays small. The reading still starts from the breach, as Rule-Keeping requires: her fondness only colours whether the breach reads as a slip or a fault, and with no breach the card does not fire. It acts on the group's conventions only; a breach that wrongs a member jars whoever commits it, and fondness does not soften it. Boundary: where a breach by one of us shames the group, harsher judgement of our own (the black sheep effect: Marques, Yzerbyt and Leyens 1988, not checked here) can outweigh it. Deck X: Warmth has one face, Rule-Keeping is hierarchical. Provisional.

forces.name: My place is defended
forces.increment_logic: When my place among the members feels secure and a call from above goes against me, I feel that those above will hear me out on it as one they keep among them: my sense that those above deal evenly with me rises a little.
forces.decrement_logic: When I am kept at the edge with no settled place among them and a call from above goes against me, I feel that no one above need hear me on it, since I am not one they keep among them: my sense that those above deal evenly with me falls.
forces.explanation: Plays only when a call from above goes against her. H twin of E:Belonging->Parity; the H deck had no route from inclusion to Parity. The lines run through her own sense of her place: a member who feels securely kept expects those above to give her a hearing, and a member at the edge expects none. What asking would cost her is Safety's ground, and being charged with stepping out of place is Face's. That step rests on common sense, with no direct test found (gap). Coalitional backing limits dominants in primates (grooming repaid in support, small effect; Schino 2007), and followers check leaders in egalitarian bands (Boehm 1993). Both are analogous to this ranked-group step and only support it. The card assumes no one actually comes to her defence; staged backing goes to interaction (I:Belonging->Parity). Play rule: where H:Belonging->Rank fires on the same scene, play this card small. Provisional, small.

forces.name: Bullying cools fondness
forces.increment_logic: When no one here can lord it over me, I am easy in their company, and my fondness for the members rises a little.
forces.decrement_logic: When a member can make me give way through fear and it goes unchecked, the company as a whole weighs on me, and my fondness for them falls.
forces.explanation: Owner-approved group-level form (Ben, 9 Nov 2026, 2.50 pm). The decrement is larger than the increment. Evidence is adjacent and at network level: removing policers left macaque grooming and play networks smaller and less integrated (Flack et al. 2006), and aggression goes with higher stress across primate studies (Fiorini-Torrico et al. 2024). The felt step in people is common sense. Reich and Hershcovis 2015 is dropped: it concerns observers' reactions to an instigator, not fondness for the members. Distinct from X:Parity->Warmth (pay gaps from above). Dislike of the coercer himself is left to interaction. Play it small where E:Parity->Belonging fires on the same scene. Provisional, small.
